ReductiveGroupsPartII.summary: Neither library contains any Bruhat–Tits theory: a whole-tree grep for `Bruhat-Tits`, `apartment`, `parahoric`, `Iwahori`, `affine root` and `building` turns up only a docstring aside in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean and the Iwahori–Hecke quadratic relation in a knot-theory file. What the libraries do supply are the ingredients: Mathlib's local-compactness theory of complete discretely valued fields with finite residue field (Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Valued/LocallyCompact.lean), the topological group GL_n(R) over a topological ring, elementary divisors over a PID, abstract root pairings with their flip (dual) and Weyl groups, and Tau Ceti's abstract Tits system with the Bruhat decomposition of a BN-pair, its split root data and root subgroup schemes for GL_n/SL_n/Sp_2n, and the identification of the R-points of the GL_n group scheme with GL_n(R). Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap actually owns: the topology on X(E) of a finite-type E-scheme, Weil restriction of affine schemes and the Deligne torus, relative roots and valued root data, buildings, parahoric and congruence group schemes, the Iwasawa/Cartan/Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions for G(E), and the pinned dual group over ℤ with its L-group. Only two of the roadmap's stated targets — the GL_n integral-points check in RG2.0 and the dual root datum input to RG2.5 — are already available.

targets.target: Topology on X(E) for a finite-type E-scheme built from affine charts, with chart independence, functoriality and compatibility with products and closed/open immersions
targets.note: No general construction of a topology on the E-points of a scheme exists in either tree. The closest analogue is Tau Ceti's monomial-embedding topology on the *complex* points of an affine semigroup scheme, which does prove exactly the chart-independence and functoriality pattern this target asks for, but only over ℂ and only for monoid algebras.

targets.target: Local compactness and Hausdorffness of X(E) for separated finite-type X over a nonarchimedean local field E
targets.note: Mathlib characterises when a rank-one valued field is locally compact (complete + discrete valuation + finite residue field) and transfers properness to finite-dimensional spaces over it, so the base case E and E^n is available; the statement for the points of a separated finite-type scheme is not, because the topology itself is not defined.

targets.target: Topological group axioms for G(E), G a finite-type affine E-group scheme
targets.note: Mathlib makes the unit group of any topological monoid a topological group and develops GL_n(R) over a topological ring, which covers G = GL_n and its closed subgroups once they carry the subspace topology; there is no statement for a general affine group scheme's E-points.

targets.target: Compactness of the integral points of an affine O_E-model
targets.note: Units of a compact T1 topological monoid form a compact space, which gives GL_n(O_E) compact once O_E is known compact; the general statement for the O_E-points of an affine flat finite-type O_E-model is absent.

targets.target: Congruence kernels give a neighbourhood basis of 1 in G(O_E) for a smooth model
targets.note: No congruence-subgroup filtration of the integral points of a group scheme exists in either tree; `congruence` in declarations.tsv matches only linear congruences, J-holomorphic congruence lemmas and Gram/quadratic-form congruence, and the classical modular Γ₀/Γ₁ subgroups, none of which are this.

targets.target: For GL_n, the integral points are GL_n(O_E) — invertible over O_E, not merely integral with nonzero determinant
targets.note: Tau Ceti identifies the A-points of the GL_n coordinate Hopf algebra R[X_ij][det⁻¹] with Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) A naturally in A, for every commutative R-algebra A and with no nontriviality hypothesis; taking A = O_E is exactly the check this target asks for, and Mathlib's isUnit_iff_isUnit_det supplies the 'det must be a unit, not merely nonzero' half. The file has no sorry.

duplicates.note: AA.0 builds the restricted-product topology and its local compactness on top of the local topological groups this layer produces; it re-proves continuity of multiplication/inversion and local compactness in the restricted-product setting rather than for X(E).
AA.1 constructs adelic points and their functoriality, taking the local topological point spaces from RG2.0.

D0 is titled 'Restriction of scalars and topological points' and applies the topological-points interface to the Deligne torus and Hilbert groups; it explicitly names RG2.0a/AA.0–AA.1 as its suppliers.

targets.target: Weil restriction (restriction of scalars) of an affine finite-type scheme along a finite locally free base map, defined by the functor T ↦ Hom_{S'}(T ×_S S', X)
targets.note: grep -rn -i for 'weil restriction', 'restriction of scalars', 'weilRestriction' and 'restrictionOfScalars' over both trees returns only module-theoretic restriction of scalars (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean, Submodule.restrictScalars, TauCeti/Algebra/Category/CommAlgCat/RestrictScalars.lean), which is the left adjoint on modules and not the Weil restriction of schemes.

targets.target: Representing algebra on a free affine chart; universal property, basis independence, descent across trivialisations, preservation of finite type and finite presentation
targets.note: Nothing in either tree constructs the coordinate ring of a Weil restriction. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves layer 0 discusses what Weil restriction does and does not represent, but as roadmap prose, not as Lean.

targets.target: Adjunction, evaluation map, products, composition and base-change isomorphisms with coherence
targets.note: Absent for the same reason: the functor itself does not exist.

targets.target: Transport of group laws; splitting-field product description for a finite separable extension; descent of smoothness, connectedness, reductivity and the torus property
targets.note: Tau Ceti can recognise a torus from a splitting field (a finite-type commutative Hopf algebra that becomes a split torus over an algebraic extension is a torus), which is the descent half of this target; but there is no Weil restriction to descend along, and no statement that Res_{L/k} of a reductive group is reductive.

targets.target: The Deligne torus S = Res_{ℂ/ℝ} G_m with S(ℝ) = ℂ^×, S_ℂ = G_m × G_m with conjugation exchanging the factors, and its norm and weight maps and character lattice
targets.note: 'Deligne torus' and 'norm torus' have zero hits in either tree; the split torus G_m and its character lattice exist in TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SplitTorus/, but S itself does not.

duplicates.note: D0 applies finite-separable Weil restriction to the Deligne torus and the Hilbert groups; its text names RG2.0a as the owner of the construction, so the overlap is consumption rather than duplication.
D1 states the same Deligne-torus targets — construct S, its diagonal and norm maps, its complex splitting with the specified conjugation, and its character lattice — as this layer's final paragraph.
A6 owns Weil restriction of non-affine abelian schemes (T_ℓ(Res_{L/K} A) ≅ Ind T_ℓ(A) and the k[ε] tangent-bundle example); complementary to, not covered by, the affine theorem here.
0G explicitly contrasts Weil restriction with the relative Grassmannian of subgroup schemes it builds, so it needs the same representability statement as an input.
ES6 constructs nonabelian Shapiro for G = Res_{E'/E} G' and so consumes the same finite-separable Weil restriction of reductive groups.

targets.target: Relative roots of G with respect to a maximal E-split torus, and the relative Weyl group
targets.note: Split (absolute) root data and abstract root pairings with Weyl groups are present in both libraries, but 'maximal split torus', 'relative root', 'anisotropic kernel' and 'quasi-split' have zero hits in either tree; the relative theory over a non-algebraically-closed field is not started.

targets.target: Root subgroups and their valuation filtrations indexed by the actual valuation sets, including nonsplit root groups
targets.note: Root subgroup schemes exist for the split classical groups and for the Kostant ℤ-form, with Chevalley commutator relations; none of them carries a valuation filtration, and there is no nonsplit or multipliable-root case.

targets.target: Multipliable roots (the non-reduced relative root system)
targets.note: Mathlib's root pairings allow non-reduced systems and Tau Ceti has TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Reduced.lean, so the abstract combinatorics of BC-type systems is available, but the group-theoretic multipliable root groups U_{(a)} ⊃ U_{2a} are not.

targets.target: Commutator estimates, conjugation by the torus, compatibility under unramified extension
targets.note: Chevalley commutator relations are proved for split SL_n/Sp_2n/GL_n root subgroups, but there is no valuation-indexed estimate [U_{a,r}, U_{b,s}] ⊆ ∏ U_{ia+jb, ir+js} and no unramified-descent statement.

targets.target: The affine root system and the apartment attached to a valued root datum
targets.note: 'affine root system' and 'affine Weyl group' occur only in a Kronecker-quiver docstring and a Mathlib Lie-loop docstring; TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/AffineDynkinType concerns affine Dynkin *diagrams* (positive-semidefinite Cartan matrices), not affine roots as functions on an apartment.

targets.target: Gluing of apartments by the Bruhat–Tits equivalence relation; well-defined affine transition maps
targets.note: No building theory of any kind in either tree.

targets.target: The building axioms and the G(E)-action on the building
targets.note: Absent; the only occurrence of 'Bruhat-Tits' in either library is a remark in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean that homothety classes of lattices in K² over a DVR give the vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree.

targets.target: Apartment existence for pairs of points; reduced versus enlarged building
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Facets, closure order, fixers, compactness modulo centre
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Fixed-point theorem for bounded subgroups
targets.note: Absent, and so is its usual ambient hypothesis: 'CAT(0)', 'nonpositive curvature' and 'Busemann' have zero hits in either tree, so there is no complete-nonpositively-curved fixed-point theorem to specialise.

targets.target: The GL_n building from homothety classes of norms/lattice chains, and the SL_2 tree
targets.note: Mathlib defines lattices in a module over the fraction field, proves they are free of the right rank and closed under intersection, and its module docstring names this as the vertex set of the Bruhat–Tits tree of GL_2(K); the homothety quotient, the simplicial structure, the norms and the tree itself are not constructed.

duplicates.note: GS0 needs affine-flag and Demazure ingredients and says parahoric models are supplied by ReductiveGroupsPartII, so it consumes rather than duplicates RG2.2–RG2.3.

targets.target: For a facet, the smooth affine O_E-group scheme with connected special fibre and prescribed root-group charts
targets.note: 'parahoric' has zero hits in either tree; no integral model of a reductive group attached to a facet exists.

targets.target: Characterisation by integral points, generic fibre G, connected reductive quotient of the special fibre, pro-unipotent radical and reduction map
targets.note: Reductivity and the unipotent radical exist over a field in Tau Ceti, so the special-fibre quotient would have a target to land in; the integral model, the reduction map and the pro-unipotent radical do not exist.

targets.target: Pro-p congruence subgroups and their compact openness
targets.note: Absent; see RG2.0's congruence-kernel target.

targets.target: Compatibility for nested facets and unramified base change; connected parahoric vs fixer group scheme vs hyperspecial model
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: GS0 names parahoric models as supplied by ReductiveGroupsPartII.

H4 constructs Iwahori and Γ₀(pⁿ) levels as subgroup-scheme conditions on the moduli problem; the same Iwahori level subgroup appears, but H4 defines it by level structures on abelian schemes rather than as a parahoric model.

targets.target: Iwasawa decomposition G(E) = P(E)·K for a special maximal compact K
targets.note: Absent in the p-adic setting. Mathlib's MulAction.IwasawaStructure (Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Iwasawa.lean) is an unrelated simplicity criterion, not the KAN/PK decomposition.

targets.target: Cartan decomposition G(E) = K · X_*(A)^+ · K with the correct relative cocharacter lattice and dominance condition
targets.note: The elementary-divisor theorem over a PID (hence over O_E) is the content of the Cartan decomposition for GL_n, but it is stated for submodules/bases and integer matrices, not as a double-coset decomposition GL_n(O)\GL_n(E)/GL_n(O) ≅ dominant cocharacters, and nothing covers a general connected reductive G.

targets.target: Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition with stabilisers
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves, sorry-free, that in any Tits system the Bruhat cells B n B cover G and that N → B\G/B is surjective, plus the rank-one multiplication law; this is exactly the abstract half of the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition. What is missing is the construction of the affine Tits system (I, N) inside G(E), hence the identification of the index set with the affine Weyl group and the stabiliser statements.

targets.target: Finiteness of compact-open double coset decompositions and index formulas
targets.note: Absent; there are no compact open subgroups of a p-adic group in either tree to decompose.

targets.target: Rank-one and nonsplit examples showing the split simply connected formula is not universal
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Layer 9 there states the Cartan and Iwasawa decompositions and KAK, but for a real reductive Lie group with maximal compact K and a Cartan involution; it is the archimedean counterpart, not the same theorem, and it shares no statement with the p-adic case beyond the name.
SR.4 (Satake) consumes exactly the Cartan decomposition and the compact-open double coset finiteness this layer proves.

targets.target: The dual root datum of the root datum of G
targets.note: Interchanging roots and coroots is Mathlib's RootPairing.flip, over any commutative ring and for any root pairing; Tau Ceti computes the induced permutation of Dynkin types (B_n ↔ C_n) with the node relabelling for F₄ and G₂. This is the combinatorial input of the layer, already present in more generality than asked.

targets.target: A pinned split group scheme over ℤ realising the dual root datum
targets.note: Tau Ceti is building the Chevalley–Demazure machinery (Kostant ℤ-form root subgroup schemes with base change and a toral closure), which is the intended route to a split group scheme over ℤ, but no existence theorem 'for every root datum there is a pinned split reductive ℤ-group' is proved, and no dual group is constructed from a datum.

targets.target: The continuous finite-image action on the pinning induced by the E-form of G
targets.note: 'pinning'/'pinned' as a group-theoretic datum has no declaration in either tree (the only matches are Geck-construction diagram symmetries and English prose).

targets.target: The semidirect L-group with projection and action law, change-of-pinning equivalence, Levi inclusions
targets.note: Only the abstract semidirect product is available; there is no L-group, no Langlands dual, and no Levi inclusion of dual groups.

targets.target: Compatibility with products, central isogenies, restriction of scalars and the split torus/GL_n examples
targets.note: Central isogenies of group schemes exist in Tau Ceti and root-datum isogenies exist in TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Isogeny, so the source side of these compatibilities is present; the dual-side statements are not, and restriction of scalars does not exist at all (see RG2.0a).

duplicates.note: GS4 reconstructs the dual group Tannakianly and then identifies it with 'the pinned dual', so it uses this layer's pinned dual group over ℤ and its Weil action as the comparison target.
LP0 constructs sections of the L-group projection and twisted conjugation, taking the L-group and its projection from RG2.5.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.summary: Tau Ceti already has the smoothness definition and the discrete/smooth dictionary that SR.0 starts from — TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete (open point stabilisers on a discrete module) for an arbitrary topological group, its equivalence with joint continuity, and an equivalence of categories with discrete G-modules — and both libraries have a sorry-free integral double-coset Hecke ring over an arbitrary coefficient semiring (Mathlib's HeckeRing/Defs.lean plus Tau Ceti's Multiplication/Associativity/Commutativity/Degree files), which is the integral-double-coset half of SR.1. Mathlib supplies further raw material: Haar measure and the modular character of a locally compact group, LocallyConstant functions, abstract induction with its adjunction, the invariants submodule, and Jacobson density / the double centralizer theorem. Everything specific to p-adic groups is missing: there is no convolution algebra of compactly supported locally constant functions, no idempotents e_U, no module-category equivalence, no smooth or compact induction, no Jacquet functor, no second adjointness, no admissibility or uniform admissibility, no Bernstein decomposition or centre, no Satake transform (the string `Satake` does not occur in either tree), and no Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives or Whittaker functionals. The abelian structure on the smooth subcategory, the smooth-vectors functor, and the exhaustion V = ⋃_U V^U for locally profinite G are also still missing, the last existing only in the profinite special case.

targets.target: Definition of a smooth representation: an algebraic action in which every vector has open stabiliser
targets.note: TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete says exactly that the underlying module is discrete and every point stabiliser {g | ρ g x = x} is open, for an arbitrary topological group G (variables at SmoothDiscrete.lean:319–320 need only [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]), so it is not restricted to profinite G. It is packaged as a property of objects of Mathlib's TopRep R G rather than of a bare Representation R G V; the file is sorry-free.

targets.target: Closure of smooth representations under subobjects, quotients, sums and filtered colimits; kernels, cokernels, and the abelian category structure
targets.note: The full representation category Rep k G is abelian in Mathlib (anonymous instance at Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Rep/Basic.lean:567, `Abelian (Rep k G) := abelianOfEquivalence (RepToAction k G)`), but nothing gives the smooth subcategory kernels, cokernels or an abelian structure: TauCeti.SmoothDiscreteTopRep is only an ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory, and grep for `Abelian` across TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology returns nothing.

targets.target: Smooth vectors of an arbitrary representation, and the adjunction with the inclusion of the smooth category
targets.note: No smoothing functor V ↦ V^∞ = ⋃_U V^U exists; grep -rn for `smoothVectors`/`smoothPart` over both trees returns nothing, and the only occurrences of `open stabilizer` are in docstrings of Galois-lattice and character-lattice files.

targets.target: For a discrete module, smoothness is equivalent to joint continuity of the action map G × V → V
targets.note: isSmoothDiscrete_iff_continuousSMul is precisely this equivalence, for any topological group; the companion lemma identifies the predicate with Mathlib's Action.IsContinuous plus discreteness, so it is the same notion as DiscreteContAction, not a second one. Proved without sorry.

targets.target: U-invariants as a submodule, with functoriality, restriction and the union description V = ⋃_U V^U over compact open U
targets.note: The invariants submodule and its comap functoriality are Mathlib's; the exhaustion ⨆_U M^U = ⊤ is proved in Tau Ceti but only for G compact and totally disconnected (the section hypotheses at Discrete.lean:173–177 are [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]), i.e. for profinite G and open normal U, not for a locally profinite group and arbitrary compact open U.

targets.target: Admissibility: finite generation of V^U for every compact open U, with stronger finiteness conditions separated
targets.note: No admissibility predicate for smooth representations exists in either tree; `admissible` matches nothing in declarations.tsv outside p-adic-Hodge `IsAdmissible`-style names, which are a different notion.

duplicates.note: R16.1 specialises this smooth-representation category, its Haar measures and its finite-level function spaces to GL₂ and explicitly names SR.0 as the sole owner of the generic definitions.
ES0 builds the algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity on 'SR.0's category', so it imports rather than restates the abelian carrier.

targets.note: LocallyConstant functions and Haar measure on a locally compact group are both in Mathlib, but there is no compactly supported locally constant function space and no convolution product on it; grep for a convolution algebra turns up only coalgebra convolution and L²-convolution on a compact group (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Convolution.lean).

targets.note: Associativity of the double-coset convolution, and the ring structure on the Hecke ring 𝕋 Δ H R over an arbitrary semiring, are proved sorry-free in Tau Ceti; what is missing is the same statement for the function-space model with measure-valued volumes, and the opposite involution.

targets.target: Normalized idempotents e_U, defined exactly when the volume/index denominators are units in A
targets.note: No idempotent attached to a compact open subgroup exists in either tree; the Hecke-ring development has a unit (HeckeRing/One.lean) but no e_U with vol(U)⁻¹.

targets.target: Equivalence between smooth representations and nondegenerate modules over the locally unital Hecke algebra, under a cofinal family of compact opens of invertible pro-order
targets.note: Absent; there is no locally unital algebra, no nondegenerate-module notion for one, and no such equivalence.

targets.note: The biinvariant objects themselves exist — HeckeCosetModule Δ H₁ H₂ Z is the module of H₁-H₂-double cosets and 𝕋 Δ H Z its diagonal ring — but nothing identifies them as corners e_U H e_U of an ambient algebra, since that algebra does not exist.

targets.target: Integral double-coset operators built from finite correspondences, where averaging is unavailable
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Hecke triple (commensurability plus Δ ≤ commensurator H₂, so double cosets are finite unions of left cosets) and the double-coset module over any coefficient ring; Tau Ceti defines the product by Shimura's multiplicities [D₁][D₂] = Σ m(D₁,D₂;D)[D] over an arbitrary semiring R and proves associativity and the ring instance, with no averaging or invertibility hypothesis. That is exactly the integral double-coset operator algebra this target asks for, in greater generality than 'compact open in a p-adic group'. All three files are sorry-free.

targets.target: Smooth induction from a closed subgroup, and compact induction with support compact modulo the subgroup
targets.note: Mathlib induces along a group homomorphism as (k[H] ⊗ A)_G with no topology anywhere; there is no smoothness or support condition, so neither smooth nor compact induction is available.

targets.target: Frobenius reciprocity with the correct adjoint direction and hypotheses
targets.note: The ind ⊣ res adjunction holds in Mathlib for abstract groups and Tau Ceti has the finite-group character form; neither is the smooth statement, where the adjoint direction depends on whether induction is smooth or compact.

targets.target: Induction in stages and Mackey filtrations
targets.note: Tau Ceti has transitivity of induction and the Mackey decomposition for finite-index/finite-group situations; the smooth Mackey filtration by double cosets in a locally profinite group, with its topological convergence issues, is absent.

targets.target: For P = MN, unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants (the unnormalized Jacquet functor)
targets.note: Coinvariants of a representation exist as a functor in Mathlib, but with no smoothness and no unipotent radical of a parabolic to take them along.

targets.target: Normalized induction and Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character
targets.note: Mathlib has the modular character of a locally compact group as a homomorphism G →* ℝ≥0, independent of the Haar measure chosen, which is the δ_P this target normalizes by; the square root, the normalized functors and their properties are absent.

targets.target: Exactness of the Jacquet functor in the valid coefficient regime, compatibility with duals for admissible representations, and the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing
targets.note: Absent; grep for `Jacquet` over both trees returns nothing, and there is no admissibility notion to state the duality compatibility against.

ES7:parabolic needs the dictionary between unnormalized parabolic induction and SR.1–SR.2's normalized induction, including the square-root modulus twist.
ET.6 develops segment/Langlands-quotient theory for GL_m from the same induction functors.

targets.target: Unit and counit of the second adjunction i_P ⊣ r_{opposite P} for complex smooth representations of a p-adic reductive group
targets.note: Absent: neither i_P nor r_P exists (see SR.2), so no adjunction between them can be stated.

targets.target: Stabilization for sufficiently contracting elements and the canonical pairing
targets.note: Absent; there is no contracting-element or Jacquet-module stabilization statement in either tree.

targets.target: Both triangle identities with the opposite parabolic and square-root normalization explicit
targets.note: Only the general notion of an adjunction with its triangle identities exists.

targets.target: The natural Hom isomorphism and compatibility with admissible contragredients
targets.note: Absent; smooth contragredients and admissibility are themselves missing.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups.summary: This is Tau Ceti's own library roadmap, and the library has built most of Layers 0–6 in the TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup tree, sorry-free (only nine files in the whole TauCeti tree contain `sorry`, none of them here). Present in full: the convolution group of points and its functor, the anti-equivalence between commutative Hopf algebras and affine group schemes with the corepresentability third leg and Hopf base change; comodules with their monoidal category, the fundamental theorem of coalgebras, matrix coefficients, faithful = closed immersion, the embedding theorem G ↪ GL_n and Tannakian reconstruction; the Lie algebra with the adjoint action, differentials, Lie subalgebras of closed subgroups and the dimension tools; Hopf ideals, normality, fppf quotient sheaves, the identity component and the finite étale component group; Jordan decomposition, diagonalizable groups with their anti-equivalence, tori and the character–cocharacter perfect pairing; geometric unipotence and the construction of the unipotent and solvable radicals; and reductive/semisimple/simply connected/adjoint with central isogenies. Genuinely missing: representability of a general quotient G/H (Matsushima), the geometric half of Lie–Kolchin (that the derived subgroup of a connected solvable group is unipotent), the characteristic-zero converse 'reductive ⇒ linearly reductive' and the characteristic-p torus criterion, conjugacy of Borel subgroups and maximal tori, the root datum of a split pair (G, T) with its coroots and Weyl group, the Galois action on the absolute root datum, the relative root system, the construction of a Tits system inside a reductive group, the whole of Layer 8's isomorphism/existence/classification theorems, and — in Layer 9 — the general definition of a pinned split reductive group scheme, the Chevalley–Demazure construction for an arbitrary root datum, the pinned isomorphism theorem, and the short-root G₂/F₄ and tripled D₄ carriers.

targets.target: R-points of a Hopf algebra as a group under convolution, with counit as identity and f ∘ S as inverse, functorial in R
targets.note: The convolution group structure is proved for an arbitrary (not necessarily commutative) Hopf algebra H over R and any commutative R-algebra value, which is more than the layer asks; pointsFunctor packages it as CommAlgCat R ⥤ GrpCat.

targets.target: Γ(G) is an R-Hopf algebra for an affine group scheme G over Spec R, and Spec A is a group object for a commutative Hopf algebra A
targets.note: hopfAlgebraGamma is the Γ-direction for a plain-typed base ring and an arbitrary structure morphism; the Spec-direction is Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.instGrpObjSpecAsOverSpec, which the file records as needing no Tau Ceti declaration.

targets.target: The anti-equivalence (CommHopfAlg k)ᵒᵖ ≌ AffGrpSch k, with finite type/smoothness kept as predicates
targets.note: Built over an arbitrary commutative base ring S from Mathlib's hopfSpec, its full faithfulness and its essential-image characterisation; object properties transport across it, so finiteness conditions stay predicates as the layer requires.

targets.target: The third equivalence with representable group functors
targets.note: The points functor is corepresented by the coordinate algebra, the contravariant points functor is fully faithful, and its essential image is exactly the group-valued functors with corepresentable underlying functor — the layer's third equivalence.

targets.target: Base change: K ⊗[k] A as a Hopf algebra over K, with the induced comparison on points
targets.note: Scalar extension is packaged functorially with the point equivalence (K ⊗[k] H →ₐ[K] A) ≃* (H →ₐ[k] A), which is what the layer needs for geometric notions after base change to k̄.

targets.target: Comodules over a coalgebra/Hopf algebra, comodule morphisms, the rigid monoidal category of finite-dimensional comodules, tensor products, duals, the regular representation
targets.note: The comodule category, the finite-dimensional point-representation category with its symmetric monoidal structure, duals (Comodule/Dual.lean) and the regular comodule (Comodule/Regular.lean) are all present.

targets.target: The fundamental theorem of comodules: every element lies in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra and every comodule is the union of its finite-dimensional subcomodules
targets.note: The elementwise fundamental theorem of coalgebras is proved over a principal ideal domain as well as over a field, so it is available in the generality the embedding theorem needs.

targets.target: The dictionary representation of G ⇆ A-comodule, and matrix coefficients
targets.note: Representations of the point group and comodules are identified as categories, and the matrix-coefficient subalgebra is developed with its finiteness.

targets.target: Faithfulness as a closed immersion G → GL(V), equivalent to the matrix coefficients generating A
targets.note: The file explicitly discharges the roadmap's 'faithfulness done right' item, and gets the subtlety right: the criterion uses the matrix coefficients together with their antipode images, since for 𝔾ₘ the coefficient T alone does not generate k[T, T⁻¹].

targets.target: The embedding theorem: every affine group scheme of finite type has a faithful finite-dimensional representation, i.e. a closed immersion into some GL_n
targets.note: Proved over a field via the fundamental theorem of coalgebras, exactly the route the layer prescribes rather than bare Noetherianity.

targets.target: Tannakian reconstruction: recover G from its tensor category of representations
targets.note: Points of the group are identified with tensor automorphisms of scalar extension on finite-dimensional comodules, for each value algebra, with naturality in the value algebra in Tannaka/GroupFunctor.lean.

duplicates.note: Only a marginal overlap: that layer's Wedderburn/central-simple material is the module-theoretic side used in complete-reducibility arguments, not the comodule dictionary.

targets.target: Tangent space at the identity, Lie(G), and the differential of a homomorphism
targets.note: The Lie algebra is the module of counit-valued derivations, with the Lie structure in Tangent/Lie/, the differential as a Lie morphism in Tangent/Lie/Map.lean, and the cotangent model.

targets.target: The Lie algebra of a closed subgroup as a Lie subalgebra
targets.note: The differential of a closed-subgroup inclusion is injective with image the derivations vanishing on the Hopf ideal; the file names this as the Layer 2 target.

targets.target: The adjoint action Ad : G → GL(Lie G)
targets.note: Conjugation in the convolution semiring restricted to derivations, packaged as a representation of the B-points on the B-valued tangent vectors, one value algebra at a time; the adjoint comodule is in Tangent/Representation.lean.

targets.target: Smoothness and dimension tools via Lie(G): dimension of kernels and the smoothness criterion
targets.note: The dimension tool the later layers actually use is that an inclusion of smooth connected closed subgroups with no gain in Lie dimension is an equality; the smoothness criterion is Cartier's smooth ⟺ geometrically reduced over an algebraically closed field.

targets.target: Hopf ideals ↔ closed subgroup schemes, the quotient Hopf algebra A/I, the anti-equivalence, and kernels
targets.note: The HopfIdeal structure (ideal with Δ(I) ⊆ I⊗A + A⊗I, ε(I) = 0, S(I) ⊆ I) lives in TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/, and the AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/ subtree develops quotients, the categorical comparison, kernels and the augmentation identification.

targets.target: Normality as stability of the Hopf ideal under the adjoint coaction, and the conjugation/adjoint morphism at Hopf level
targets.note: Normality is available with base change, images, common kernels and products.

targets.target: The quotient G/H as an fppf sheaf, with representability as a theorem with hypotheses (Matsushima for H reductive)
targets.note: The fppf quotient sheaf with its universal property is constructed, and the quotient by the identity component is shown representable by the constant component group scheme; but the file states plainly that 'no representability is asserted' in general, and `Matsushima` has zero hits in either tree, so the affineness criterion for H reductive is absent.

targets.target: Short exact sequences of affine group schemes
targets.note: Kernels, images and the quotient projection exist separately, but there is no packaged short-exact-sequence notion for affine group schemes and no exactness theorem relating the three.

targets.target: Identity component G° and component group π₀(G), with geometric connectedness and finite étaleness of π₀ under smoothness
targets.note: Geometric connectedness is defined by absence of nontrivial idempotents after base change to the algebraic closure, as the layer asks; the component group is the constant group scheme on π₀(Spec H) over an algebraically closed field, proved finite and étale.

targets.target: Multiplicative Jordan decomposition of points into semisimple and unipotent parts, functorial under representations
targets.note: Constructed for K-valued points over a perfect extension field via Tannakian reconstruction, so the two parts stay inside the group rather than in each ambient GL_n; naturality is in JordanDecomposition/Naturality.lean.

targets.target: Diagonalizable groups and groups of multiplicative type: the anti-equivalence M ↦ D(M) = Spec k[M] between finitely generated abelian groups and diagonalizable groups
targets.note: The contravariant equivalence from FGCommGrpCatᵒᵖ is constructed, with the character lattice, closed subgroups, weights and Frobenius developed alongside; groups of multiplicative type have their own subtree.

targets.target: μ_n = D(ℤ/n), 𝔾_m = D(ℤ), and the non-smooth example μ_p in characteristic p
targets.note: μ_n and 𝔾_m are constructed with their points; the non-smoothness of μ_p is the non-reducedness of its coordinate ring, which combines with smooth ⟺ reduced over an algebraically closed field to give the stated example.

targets.target: Tori, split and non-split, with the character lattice X*(T), the cocharacter lattice X_*(T) and their perfect pairing
targets.note: Non-split tori are recognised from a splitting field, and the character/cocharacter lattices with their Galois action and invariant perfect pairing are in MultiplicativeType/GaloisModule.lean; the perfect pairing instance is proved for split tori.

targets.target: The geometric definition of unipotence (ρ_g − id nilpotent in every finite-dimensional representation) and the embedding of a smooth connected unipotent group in U_n
targets.note: The definition is exactly the comodule-level one the layer insists on (nilpotence of ρ_g − 1 on every finite-dimensional comodule), avoiding the vacuous reduced-ring version; the embedding into upper unitriangular matrices is Unipotent/Embedding.lean and UpperUnitriangular/.

targets.target: Lie–Kolchin: a connected solvable group is trigonalizable
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the representation-theoretic half: if the derived subgroup has only unipotent points then every nonzero finite-dimensional comodule has a weight vector and is upper-triangularizable. Its own docstring records the missing step: 'the derived subgroup of a connected solvable affine group is unipotent'. So Lie–Kolchin as stated is not yet available.

targets.target: Solvable groups
targets.note: Solvability of the point group, its behaviour under base change, extensions, normal products and semidirect products, and its reduction to the derived subgroup are all proved.

targets.target: The unipotent radical R_u(G): the maximal connected normal unipotent closed subgroup, with the distinction between the k-unipotent radical and the geometric one over imperfect fields
targets.note: Constructed by the maximal-Lie-dimension argument plus product closure, with a choice-free universal property; the construction file states explicitly that over a nonperfect field this is the k-unipotent radical and makes no claim that it commutes with base change to k̄, which is the caveat the layer flags.

targets.target: Reductive: smooth, connected, with trivial geometric unipotent radical; semisimple: trivial radical
targets.note: Both predicates are defined through a shared geometric normal-subgroup-freeness construction, so they are available without choosing a maximal subgroup; the semisimple definition correctly requires smoothness of the candidate subgroup.

targets.target: The radical R(G), the centre Z(G), the derived group G_der
targets.note: All three are constructed as Hopf ideals with their base-change, functoriality, smoothness and connectedness properties; the centre is scheme-theoretic, detecting infinitesimal centres rather than only rational points.

targets.target: Central isogenies, and the simply connected and adjoint forms
targets.note: Isogenies are finite faithfully flat coordinate morphisms with central kernel, defined over an arbitrary base and bridged to the scheme side; simple connectivity and adjointness are the expected properties of semisimple groups. No existence statement (that every semisimple group has a simply connected cover) is proved.

targets.target: Linearly reductive as an alternative characterization, with the characteristic-zero equivalence reductive ⇔ linearly reductive and the characteristic-p statement that a connected linearly reductive group over an algebraically closed field is a torus
targets.note: Linear reductivity is defined and one direction of the Layer 6 comparison is proved — a smooth geometrically connected finite-type group whose geometric fibre is linearly reductive is reductive, via triviality of normal unipotent subgroups — and a diagonalizable group is linearly reductive. The characteristic-zero converse is stated in the source file as 'a separate development' and is not proved, and the characteristic-p criterion (connected linearly reductive ⟺ torus) is only quoted in a docstring.

duplicates.note: RG2.3 needs the connected reductive quotient of a parahoric's special fibre, which is a consumer of this layer's reductivity predicate over a field.

targets.target: Borel subgroups and maximal tori, and their conjugacy
targets.note: Existence of a Borel subgroup over the algebraic closure and of maximal tori is proved by the maximal-Lie-dimension argument; both source files say explicitly that 'no conjugacy statement is proved here', so the conjugacy half of this target is missing.

targets.target: Parabolic subgroups and the Levi decomposition
targets.note: The dynamic method the layer names as the preferred parallel route is fully developed: P(λ), Z(λ), U(λ) on the functor of points, the limit retraction, and the semidirect-product Levi decomposition U(λ) ⋊ Z(λ) ≃ P(λ) at every value algebra.

targets.target: The root datum (X*(T), Φ, X_*(T), Φ^∨) of (G, T) with its Weyl group, in the split case
targets.note: The roots of a split pair are available as the nontrivial weights of the adjoint representation restricted along a diagonalizable subgroup, and the file says so in as many words; but there is no construction of the coroots of a general split pair and hence no root datum of (G, T), only the explicit diagonal root datum of GL_n and the abstract root pairings of Mathlib and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem.

targets.target: The absolute root datum with Galois action, and the relative root system for non-split groups
targets.note: The Galois action on the character and cocharacter lattices of a torus exists, which is the lattice half; there is no Galois action on a root datum, and 'relative root' has zero hits in either tree.

targets.target: Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems
targets.note: The abstract theory is done: a Tits system with its axioms, the Bruhat cells covering the group, surjectivity of N → B\G/B, the rank-one multiplication law and subword expansion, all sorry-free. What is missing is the construction of a Tits system inside a reductive group from its Borel and torus normaliser, which is what the layer asks for.

duplicates.note: RG2.1 owns the relative roots and valued root data over a local field, which is the relative half named here; the two layers state the same relative root system, with RG2.1 adding the valuation.
RG2.4 proves the Bruhat and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions for G(E); this layer owns the abstract BN-pair theory they specialise.

targets.target: The isomorphism theorem: split reductive groups are classified by their root data
targets.note: Absent; there is no root datum of a general split pair to classify by (see Layer 7), and no isomorphism theorem is stated anywhere.

targets.target: Classification of semisimple groups by Dynkin diagrams
targets.note: The Cartan–Killing classification is developed on the root-system side (a base has at most one valid Dynkin type, with the B/C and D₃ coincidences handled), but nothing attaches a Dynkin diagram to a semisimple group or classifies groups by it.

targets.target: Central isogenies and the isogeny theorem
targets.note: Both sides exist — central isogenies of group schemes and isogenies of root pairings — but the isogeny theorem relating them is not proved.

targets.target: Chevalley existence: every root datum is realised by a split reductive group
targets.note: Absent. Layer 9 constructs pieces of the Chevalley–Demazure machinery over ℤ, but no existence theorem for an arbitrary root datum is proved; grep for 'Chevalley existence' matches only a docstring of Lie/Sl2/Associative.lean saying a pinned group is wanted rather than an existence theorem.

targets.target: Relative theory over a base and pseudo-reductive groups (Conrad–Gabber–Prasad)
targets.note: Absent; 'pseudo-reductive'/'pseudoreductive' occurs only as a bibliography entry in the dynamic-method files, and there is no reductive group scheme over a general base.

duplicates.note: Layer 9 explicitly carves the split-over-ℤ case out of this layer's Chevalley existence, and says the existence theorem here cannot be Classical.choose-d into a carrier.

targets.target: Split reductive group schemes over a base (at least over ℤ), with the split maximal torus as data
targets.note: No definition of a split reductive group scheme over a base exists; what exists is the weight torus 𝔾ₘ^κ ⟶ GL_n of an explicit Kostant carrier, which supplies the torus for each individual carrier but not the general notion.

targets.target: Pinnings (G, T, B, {X_α}) as data
targets.note: Every explicit carrier carries its pinning equations t(s) x_i(u) t(s)⁻¹ = x_{α_i}(s) u, and a Borel is identified for SL (UpperTriangular.lean); but there is no bundled `Pinning` structure and the data is repeated per carrier.

targets.target: The Chevalley–Demazure construction: for each root datum, an explicitly constructed split reductive group scheme over ℤ via a Chevalley basis and the Kostant ℤ-form
targets.note: The starting root data exist for every Dynkin type, the Kostant ℤ-form of the enveloping algebra and its root subgroup group schemes over ℤ are constructed with base change, closed immersion, tangent and relation files, and the toral closure of a module is built; what is not there is the assembly of these into a single split reductive group scheme attached to an arbitrary root datum.

targets.target: Base change along ℤ → k and compatibility of the pinning with it
targets.note: Base change of the generated subgroup scheme and of the root subgroup coordinate maps is proved, and the toral-closure carriers have their own BaseChange and GeneralLinearBaseChange files.

targets.target: Root subgroup maps x_α : 𝔾_a → G with the Chevalley commutator relations and the pinning equations
targets.note: Root subgroup maps and the Chevalley commutator relations are proved both for the Kostant construction (Scheme/Relations, MultiplyLacedRelations) and for the classical carriers SL_n, GL_n and Sp_2n.

targets.target: Points over an algebraically closed field as a group, functorially in the field, with the q-power Frobenius
targets.note: The q-power Frobenius on the elementary group and the Steinberg composite γ ∘ Frob_q are constructed with their defining equations on root subgroups; the Steinberg file is explicit that identifying the fixed points with a finite group of Lie type needs the pinned ambient data that does not yet exist.

targets.target: The isomorphism theorem for pinned groups: an isomorphism of root data lifts uniquely to an isomorphism of pinned group schemes
targets.note: Absent, and the library says so: Kostant/RootSubgroup/NumberedSymmetry.lean records that it is not the isomorphism theorem for pinned groups and that no uniqueness statement is claimed.

targets.target: Special isogenies in characteristics two and three for B₂/C₂ and F₄ (p = 2) and G₂ (p = 3), with τ² = Frob_p and the action on long and short root subgroups
targets.note: The rank-two symplectic case is done, with the square relation and the action on the four simple root subgroups, and the root-datum-level special isogeny is selected for every Suzuki–Ree index with its convention checked; the G₂ and F₄ group-scheme maps are not there — TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/G2/ShortRoot and F4/ShortRoot contain only the integral Lie-algebra representations (7- and 26-dimensional).

targets.target: Explicit carriers with numbered symmetries: the short-root G₂ and F₄ carriers and the tripled D₄ (triality) carrier
targets.note: The doubled E₆ carrier with its graph automorphism exists and is the model the layer points at, and the G₂/F₄ short-root modules exist as integral Lie-algebra representations; the toral-closure group-scheme carriers inside GL₇, GL₂₆ and GL₂₄, and the tripled D₄ carrier with triality, do not ('triality' has no hits in the Lie tree).

duplicates.note: The CFSG statement roadmap's L0 is the consumer this layer exists for; it states the same ambient pinned groups with root subgroups and the same explicit carriers, which is why the roadmap warns against a bare existence theorem.
RG2.5 needs a pinned split group scheme over ℤ for the dual group; this layer is the construction it would use, on the other side of the duality.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.summary: Neither library proves Ado's theorem or Iwasawa's: `Ado` has no hit in either tree, and there is no faithful finite-dimensional representation theorem for an abstract finite-dimensional Lie algebra. What is present is a large part of the substrate. Mathlib supplies LieModule.IsFaithful with its dictionary lemmas, Algebra.lmul_injective, the universal enveloping algebra with its universal property, LieDerivation, LieAlgebra.SemiDirectSum, the solvable radical, maxNilpotentIdeal (the largest ideal acting nilpotently, not the roadmap's nil L), Engel's theorem, Lie's theorem for triangularizable modules, Lie base change and — exactly as Layer 7 asks — the Krull intersection theorem Ideal.mem_iInf_smul_pow_eq_bot_iff. Tau Ceti supplies the PBW filtration, its associated graded algebra and comparison map, the spanning half of the ordered-monomial theorem, the Casimir element, and Weyl's complete reducibility over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Genuinely missing: the full PBW basis (linear independence) and hence injectivity of ι for a general Lie algebra, U(L) as a domain and as a Noetherian ring, the augmentation ideal of U(L) and the weighted truncation, noncommutative derivations and the lifting of a LieDerivation to U(L), nil L and its behaviour under derivations, Levi decomposition, central p-polynomials and module-finiteness over them, and every assembled theorem of Layers 5, 8 and 9.

targets.target: Faithfulness dictionary: injectivity of ρ, triviality of its kernel and LieModule.IsFaithful are equivalent, with constructors both ways
targets.note: IsFaithful is defined as injectivity of toEnd and carries the mk_iff form plus isFaithful_iff' (x acts as 0 ⇒ x = 0) and toEnd_eq_zero_iff, i.e. the three equivalent forms the layer asks for, with the subalgebra instance as one of the constructors.

targets.target: Left-regular representation: Algebra.lmul is injective, so an injective Lie map L → A into a finite-dimensional associative algebra gives a faithful finite-dimensional representation
targets.note: Left multiplication is an injective algebra map A →ₐ End R A for any unital algebra, and the commutator Lie structure on an associative algebra is Mathlib's; the composite statement is one line from these but is not itself recorded.

targets.target: Finite-target reduction: q : U(L) →ₐ A with q ∘ ι injective gives Ado's representation, and conversely a faithful finite-dimensional representation extends to U(L) → End V; the equivalence
targets.note: The universal property (lift) and the canonical map ι exist, so the 'conversely' half is immediate; the packaged equivalence and the forward reduction are not stated.

targets.target: Direct sums separate finitely many directions: the kernel of a finite direct sum of representations is the intersection of the kernels
targets.note: Kernels of Lie homomorphisms exist, but there is no statement computing the kernel of a direct sum of Lie representations as an intersection, and no assembly of finitely many representations into a faithful one.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.summary: Tau Ceti has built almost all of this roadmap, sorry-free, in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/ and the supporting Induction/ tree: class functions with their conjugacy-class indexing and the nondegenerate character pairing; class sums as a basis of the centre of k[G] with computable structure constants and their integrality; Artin–Wedderburn with the centre splitting and #irreducibles = #classes; the orthonormal basis of irreducible characters, primitive central idempotents, the virtual-character lattice, the character table with second (column) orthogonality and labelled uniqueness; the arithmetic of character values including cyclotomic integrality, central-character integrality, χ(1) ∣ |G|, the Galois power action and Burnside's p^a q^b theorem; the Dixon–Schneider specification with its class-multiplication matrices and eigenrow characterisation; an executable Burnside–Dixon–Schneider solver with certified primes for D₄, D₃, Q₈, C₃, S₄ and A₄ and an unconditional soundness theorem; the Frobenius–Schur indicator with the full trichotomy, real realizability and the involution count; and Frobenius's theorem with its T.I. isometry and exceptional characters. What is genuinely missing is small and specific: Brauer's theorem that ℚ(ζ_e) is a splitting field, the verified coefficient bound that would make the Dixon search provably complete (the library flags this explicitly as unverified), and, in Layer 9, the cuspidal series GL2Cuspidal and the assembled GL₂(𝔽_q) character table — the conjugacy classification, the linear, Steinberg and principal-series rows and their values are there.

targets.target: ClassFunction k G as a submodule of G → k, containing every character
targets.note: Both the Representation-level and FDRep-level characters are packaged as class functions, with eq_of_isConj as the membership criterion.

targets.target: ClassFunction k G ≃ₗ (ConjClasses G → k), hence finrank = Nat.card (ConjClasses G) for finite G
targets.note: Exactly the statement that makes the character table square.

targets.target: The character pairing (Nat.card G)⁻¹ • ∑ g, f₁ g * f₂ g⁻¹: bilinear, symmetric, nondegenerate, with the conjugation relation over ℂ and orthonormality of irreducible characters
targets.note: Nondegeneracy and symmetry are proved for the bilinear pairing, the f(g⁻¹) = conj (f g) relation for virtual characters is separate as the layer asks, and char_orthonormal appears as orthonormality of the irreducible characters for characterPairing.

targets.target: The class sum classSum k C = ∑_{g ∈ C} g as a computable def
targets.note: Defined on Fintype/DecidableEq data and proved central.

targets.target: The class sums form a basis of the centre of k[G], so finrank Z(k[G]) = Nat.card (ConjClasses G) and the centre is commutative
targets.note: The centre is free on the class sums, with the dimension count the character table needs.

targets.target: Structure constants a_{ijk} as a computable ℕ-valued function, with classSum Cᵢ * classSum Cⱼ = ∑ₖ aᵢⱼₖ • classSum Cₖ and the coercion lemmas
targets.note: Representative-independence is built into the definition through the fibre equivalence, and the defining identity is proved both in k[G] and in the centre.

targets.target: The integral class centre: each class sum is integral over ℤ
targets.note: Integrality is proved for the class sum both in k[G] and in the centre, which is what the central-character integrality argument of Layer 4 consumes.

targets.target: k[G] ≅ ∏ᵢ Mat_{nᵢ}(k) over an algebraically closed k with char ∤ |G|, and ∑ nᵢ² = |G|
targets.note: Composed from Maschke and Mathlib's Artin–Wedderburn over an algebraically closed field, exactly as the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Irreducible-indexing infrastructure: a type of isomorphism classes of simple k[G]-modules with character and degree, and the equivalence with the Wedderburn block index
targets.note: Indexing is by the irreducible characters (with characterDegree and irreducibleRepresentation), and the block ⇆ simple-module dictionary is IrreducibleClassification.lean; the roadmap's abstract `Irreps k G` type is realised concretely rather than as a fresh type, which is a presentational difference only.

targets.target: The centre splits: Z(k[G]) ≃ₐ (Irreps → k) by central characters, so central characters separate points
targets.note: The sharp separation form Layer 5 needs is proved.

targets.target: #irreducibles = #conjugacy classes
targets.note: Proved by combining the centre splitting with Layer 1's dimension count, as the layer directs.

duplicates.note: The semisimple-algebras roadmap owns the block ⇆ simple-module dictionary this layer may consume; the roadmap text says it is not a prerequisite for the Wedderburn step itself.

targets.target: Completeness: the irreducible characters are an orthonormal basis of ClassFunction k G
targets.note: Spanning, linear independence (Independence.lean) and the resulting basis are all present.

targets.target: Primitive central idempotents, their class-sum expansion, orthogonality eᵢeⱼ = δᵢⱼeᵢ, ∑ eᵢ = 1, and the Wedderburn projector property
targets.note: Constructed as (χ(1)/|G|) • ∑_g χ(g⁻¹) • g with the class-sum expansion, orthogonality, completeness of the family and injectivity.

targets.target: The virtual-character lattice VirtualCharacter G with its integer-valued pairing
targets.note: The ℤ-span of the irreducible characters is built as a ring (closed under products, containing 1) inside the class functions, which is the arena Layer 4's Galois action uses.

targets.target: The character table as a square matrix with first column the degrees and ∑ nᵢ² = |G|
targets.note: Well-definedness on representatives comes from the class-function packaging.

targets.target: Second (column) orthogonality with the class-size weights
targets.note: Derived from completeness of the class-function basis, with the |G|/|C| weight, exactly as the layer requires rather than by a rescaling argument.

targets.target: Labelled uniqueness: the table is determined up to a permutation of rows only
targets.note: Stated with columns indexed by the actual conjugacy classes, as the layer insists.

targets.target: Diagonalizability of ρ g and the description of χ(g) as a sum of e-th roots of unity
targets.note: Both arenas of the layer are present: semisimplicity over a general k with char ∤ |G|, and the root-of-unity sum where X^e − 1 splits.

targets.target: Character values are cyclotomic integers: IsIntegral ℤ (χ g) and membership in ℤ[ζ_e]
targets.note: Stated over ℂ as the layer directs, not over an arbitrary field.

targets.target: Central characters as algebra homomorphisms Z(k[G]) → k with ω_χ(Kⱼ) = |Cⱼ|χ(gⱼ)/χ(1), and integrality of ω_χ on class sums
targets.note: The formula and the integrality route through the integral class centre are both present.
Proved by the algebraic-integer plus Galois-invariance argument the layer describes.

targets.target: The Galois action of (ZMod e)ˣ on virtual characters by (σ_k · χ)(g) = χ(g^k), permuting the irreducibles, with the field of values
targets.note: That Galois acts by the power maps — the statement Layer 6's lift needs — is proved here, at both the Representation and FDRep levels.

targets.target: Brauer: ℚ(ζ_e) is a splitting field, i.e. every irreducible ℂ-representation is realizable over it
targets.note: Tau Ceti has reduced Brauer's induction theorem to the single membership 1 ∈ V_G and has Artin's theorem (Induction/Artin/), but neither Brauer's induction theorem nor the splitting-field consequence is proved. The layer marks this as an application off the critical path.

targets.target: Burnside's p^a q^b theorem, via central-character integrality and the vanishing lemma
targets.note: The full theorem is proved, together with the vanishing lemma it rests on, and in the sharper divisibility form as well.

targets.target: The coordinate identity ω_χ(Kᵢ)ω_χ(Kⱼ) = ∑ₖ aᵢⱼᵏ ω_χ(Kₖ)
targets.note: Proved before the eigenvector theorem, as the layer asks.

targets.target: Class-multiplication matrices with a pinned convention, their commutativity, and the eigenrow characterisation of central characters
targets.note: The matrices, their commutativity (from commutativity of the centre) and injectivity are proved, and the central-character rows are the common eigenrows; the convention is pinned in the API rather than in prose.

targets.target: Normalization at the identity class and degree recovery d_χ² = |G| / ∑ⱼ |Cⱼ|⁻¹ ω(Kⱼ)ω(Kⱼ⁻¹), with the conversion between the central table Ω and the ordinary table X
targets.note: Both directions of the Ω ⇆ X conversion are present, with the centralCharacterRow normalized at the identity class.

targets.target: IsCharacterTableSpec G X, the theorem that characterTable G satisfies it, and labelled uniqueness
targets.note: The specification, its satisfaction by the real table and uniqueness up to row permutation are all proved, which is exactly what makes Layer 6's output 'the' table.

targets.target: Exact cyclotomic arithmetic: the computable ring ℤ[X]/Φ_e with +, *, DecidableEq, an embedding into ℂ and reduction to ZMod p
targets.note: Built as coefficient vectors on the power basis, with the lift and residue machinery in CharacterTable/Dixon/Lift.lean.

targets.target: Executable class data with an equivalence to ConjClasses G and an executable structureConstant
targets.note: ClassData with its worked instances for cyclic, dihedral, quaternion, symmetric-four and alternating-four groups.

targets.target: Computable finite-field linear algebra: kernelBasis by verified Gaussian elimination and eigenvalueSearch
targets.note: The kernel basis is built from a verified echelon form with span and independence proofs; the layer called this 'the one linear-algebra gap on the critical path' and it is closed.

targets.target: Certified Dixon prime data and IsGoodDixonPrime, with certified primes for the worked examples and the separate existence theorem
targets.note: Both halves are done: explicit certified data for D₄, D₃, Q₈, C₃ and A₄, and the separate (noncomputable) existence theorem the layer asked to keep out of any #eval.

targets.target: The good-prime structure theorem: Z(𝔽_p[G]) ≃ₐ 𝔽_p^r with exactly r algebra homomorphisms
targets.note: Proved in FiniteField.lean for the centre over a finite field and specialised at a good Dixon prime, with the count of modular central characters.

targets.target: The eigenvector search over ZMod p refining to one-dimensional common eigenspaces, output the reduced central table
targets.note: The modular eigenrow predicate and the search are implemented and related to the algebra homomorphisms.

targets.target: The structured cyclotomic lift liftCyclotomic from the residue tuple over (ZMod e)ˣ plus a bounded-coefficient certificate, with uniqueness
targets.note: The lift and its uniqueness are proved conditionally on the coordinate bound |c| ≤ ⌊√|G|⌋; the file states in as many words that whether the coordinates the algorithm reconstructs really satisfy that bound 'is unverified, it is proved nowhere in this repository'. So the certificate is a hypothesis rather than a theorem.

targets.target: The assembled solver characterTableDixon G with a certificate, and the summit theorem that its image in ℂ is the character table
targets.note: The solver exists in both the rational and the exact-cyclotomic staging, returns an Option, and its soundness — every returned table satisfies IsCharacterTableSpec after embedding into ℂ, hence is the character table by Layer 5's uniqueness — is unconditional. What is missing is completeness: that at a good Dixon prime the search succeeds, which needs the unverified coefficient bound above. The staged examples reach A₄; A₅ is not among them.

targets.target: The Frobenius–Schur indicator |G|⁻¹ ∑_g χ(g²) at the Representation and FDRep levels, and their agreement
targets.note: Mathlib has no Frobenius–Schur indicator, and the layer says so; Tau Ceti builds it, with its expression as a difference of invariant dimensions.

targets.target: Symmetric and exterior squares of a representation with the character formulas χ_{Sym²}(g) = ½(χ(g)² + χ(g²)) and χ_{Λ²}(g) = ½(χ(g)² − χ(g²))
targets.note: Built as the layer asks, with the doubled forms available for characteristic-free use.

targets.target: Invariant bilinear forms as the G-invariants of V* ⊗ V*, splitting into symmetric and alternating with the multiplicity computation
targets.note: The invariant-form space is computed and split into its symmetric and alternating parts with their dimensions.

targets.target: The trichotomy ν₂(χ) ∈ {+1, 0, −1} with the orthogonal/symplectic/complex characterisation
targets.note: The three cases and their form-theoretic characterisations are proved for irreducible complex representations.

targets.target: Realizability over ℝ: the predicate IsRealForm and the theorem that ν₂ = 1 makes ρ realizable over ℝ
targets.note: Both directions are proved, so the stronger target the layer separated out is also discharged.

targets.target: The involution-counting formula #{g : g² = x} = ∑_χ ν₂(χ) χ(x)
targets.note: The degree-weighted form is proved; the unweighted count is kept separate as the layer requires.

targets.target: Real classes and the equality of the number of real-valued irreducible characters with the number of real conjugacy classes
targets.note: Proved through the inversion-invariance count.

targets.target: The Frobenius complement: a proper nontrivial trivial-intersection (malnormal) subgroup
targets.note: Defined exactly as proper, nontrivial and meeting each distinct conjugate trivially.

targets.target: The Frobenius kernel as a set, bundled as a normal subgroup complementing H, so G = N ⋊ H
targets.note: Frobenius's theorem is proved with the bundled subgroup and the exact names the layer prescribes.

targets.target: The T.I.-set machinery: IsTISet and the induction isometry for class functions supported on H#
targets.note: The load-bearing norm-preservation lemma is proved in the stated form, not the weaker tautology.

targets.target: The exceptional-character correspondence and the class function cutting out N
targets.note: The exceptional characters and the normality of the resulting kernel are both proved.

targets.target: Consequences: |H| ∣ |N| − 1
targets.note: The divisibility |H| ∣ |N| − 1 follows from the complement structure, which is proved; the layer marks Thompson's nilpotence as a downstream target that it does not prove, and it is indeed absent.

targets.note: The class count q² − 1 is proved in Tau Ceti's GL₂ conjugacy-class file (with the normal-form classification in NormalForm.lean), and the group order is Mathlib's.

targets.note: The length-two decomposition at α = β, the Steinberg representation, its dimension q and its irreducibility (with twists) are all proved.

targets.note: The non-split torus and the class function induced from a character of it are constructed, with its values on the four class families; but `GL2Cuspidal` has no hit in declarations.tsv, so the cuspidal representation itself, its dimension q − 1 and the θ ∼ θ^q parametrisation are not yet there.

targets.note: The linear, Steinberg and principal-series rows have their values on all four families; the cuspidal row does not exist yet.

targets.note: Absent; no assembled GL₂ character table and no completeness tally exist, and the degenerate q = 2 case is not separately treated.
